The indicator function $1[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false.

$$
1[P]=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }P\text{ is true}, \\ 0, & \text{if }P\text{ is false}.\end{aligned}
$$

The expression $1[{x}_{i}\ge 0]\cdot ({x}_{i}-1)+1[{x}_{i}<0]\cdot 2$ equals ${x}_{i}-1$ when ${x}_{i}\ge 0$ and equals $2$ when ${x}_{i}<0.$ Thus, the sum

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}\ge 0]\cdot ({x}_{i}-1)+1[{x}_{i}<0]\cdot 2
$$

adds ${x}_{i}-1$ for nonnegative values and $2$ for negative values.

We evaluate the indicator function for each ${x}_{i}:$

- $1[{x}_{1}\ge 0]=1[-3\ge 0]=0,$ $1[{x}_{1}<0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{2}\ge 0]=1[1\ge 0]=1,$ $1[{x}_{2}<0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{3}\ge 0]=1[6\ge 0]=1,$ $1[{x}_{3}<0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{4}\ge 0]=1[-2\ge 0]=0,$ $1[{x}_{4}<0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{5}\ge 0]=1[0\ge 0]=1,$ $1[{x}_{5}<0]=0$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}\ge 0]\cdot ({x}_{i}-1)+1[{x}_{i}<0]\cdot 2 & =2+(1-1)+(6-1)+2+(0-1) \\  & =2+0+5+2-1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
